claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic CoCrFeNi.
The starting CoCrFeNi is as-cast, fully annealed, and microstructurally homogeneous.
Powder-metallurgy blending and hot pressing can produce a uniform dispersion of 10 vol% CaF2 nanoparticles in CoCrFeNi.
Adding 10 vol% CaF2 nanoparticles will produce a continuous CaF2 tribofilm across the sliding contact.
The continuous CaF2 tribofilm will form during sliding in air throughout 25–800 °C.
Contact stress and temperature cause CaF2 nanoparticles to migrate to the sliding interface.
Interfacial CaF2 develops a stable, low-shear film.
The CaF2 film inhibits adhesive wear.
The CaF2 film inhibits oxidative wear.
The intervention will reduce coefficient of friction by at least 30% relative to pure CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature from 25 to 800 °C.
The intervention will reduce wear rate by at least tenfold relative to pure CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature from 25 to 800 °C.
The composite coefficient of friction will remain below 0.4 at all tested temperatures.
The composite wear rate at 800 °C will remain below 1×10^-5 mm^3/(N·m).
The composite wear rate at 25 °C will remain below 1×10^-6 mm^3/(N·m).
Pure CoCrFeNi has a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.3 at 25 °C and greater than 0.6 at 800 °C.
Pure CoCrFeNi wear rate increases from approximately 1×10^-6 mm^3/(N·m) at 25 °C to approximately 1×10^-4 mm^3/(N·m) at 800 °C.
The specified comparison will be conducted in laboratory air at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C, using a 5 N load, 0.1 m/s sliding speed, and 1000 m sliding distance.
The proposed performance is valid in approximately 21% O2 air over loads of 2–10 N, sliding speeds of 0.05–0.2 m/s, and temperatures of 25–800 °C.

contradictions.description: At 25 °C, the baseline wear rate is stated as approximately 1×10^-6 mm^3/(N·m), while the composite is only predicted to remain below 1×10^-6 mm^3/(N·m). Those values do not establish the separately claimed tenfold wear-rate reduction, which would require approximately 1×10^-7 mm^3/(N·m) or lower.

A coefficient of friction below 0.4 does not by itself establish a 30% reduction at 25 °C relative to the stated baseline of approximately 0.3; a 30% reduction there would require a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.21 or lower.
